The test image shows a corn plant with abnormal growth at the top — excessive proliferation of small shoots/tillers emerging from the growing point, rather than a normal tassel. The leaves are generally green with no obvious lesions or pustules. This pattern of vegetative proliferation strongly suggests Crazy Top or possibly Head Smut.

Let me check reference images for my top candidates.

This is a very strong match. The Crazy_Top reference (Corn_Disease_72) shows the exact same characteristic: excessive proliferation of small, twisted leafy shoots replacing the normal tassel — identical to the test image pattern.

Let me check Head Smut to rule it out.
Head Smut shows dark smut masses — very different from the green leafy proliferation in the test image. I need one more reference from a different class to complete my budget.

Corn Stunt Spiroplasma shows purple/necrotic ear tissue — completely different from the test image.

**Summary of evidence:**
- Test image: corn plant with excessive proliferation of small, narrow leafy shoots from the top (tassel area replaced by vegetative growth), viewed from below
- Crazy_Top ref (Corn_Disease_72): near-identical — classic "crazy top" symptom of tassel replaced by mass of proliferating leafy shoots
- Head Smut: dark smut masses, not matching
- Corn Stunt Spiroplasma: ear discoloration, not matching

The test image is a textbook Crazy Top case.
